Subject: Proposed Order Form (pricing schedule + net terms)

Ben —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Procurement here — attached is the order form draft AcmeTech is pushing from our side (orderform_proposed_v1.docx). High level points we need covered before legal will sign:

- Net45 on invoices (billing team requires 45-day payment window).
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up against actual usage, with credits/charges applied to the following quarter.
- VAT: we are in an EU subsidiary. We will provide VAT residency evidence but request a reverse-charge language in the order form rather than Redwood collecting VAT.
- Minimum commit: request the first-year minimum commit be prorated to align with our fiscal quarter start (we want the initial term to start 05/01 and true-up quarter thereafter).

Please loop in finance and legal from your side. We can sign once the net terms and VAT language are clarified and we receive the updated SF order form.

Attachments: orderform_proposed_v1.docx (docx, 220KB)

Regards,
Oliver

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick responses and next steps from our side: 

1) Net terms: Redwood standard is Net30. We can consider Net45 if AcmeTech can accept a small concession on upfront credits or an invoice-apply schedule — happy to propose options.

2) True-up cadence: Quarterly true-up is fine; we need to lock the definition (calendar quarter vs fiscal quarter) and the lookback window for usage. Karthik, can you prepare a pricing table showing quarterly true-up examples?

3) VAT: we will need AcmeTech's VAT/residency certificate to justify reverse-charge. If you can attach that, Kim (legal) will review and confirm language.

4) Minimum commit proration: we typically prorate to the effective date; if you want the term to align to 05/01 we can handle that but need to adjust invoice triggers.

I've attached a pricing snapshot that shows a few true-up scenarios for FY1 vs FY2.

Attachments: pricing_table_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 64KB)

I'll loop Legal to redline the order form text for the VAT and net terms. If we can lock these items this week we can route for DocuSign next week.

Oliver / Ben —

Thanks — I reviewed AcmeTech's proposed doc and prepared a short redline summary. Key legal positions: 

- VAT / Reverse-charge: Redwood will accept reverse-charge language where supported by jurisdiction and supported by submitted VAT/residency evidence. We will not automatically treat the order form as VAT-exempt without that proof. Please provide the certificate and the EU VAT registration number.

- Net terms: Our revenue recognition and cash forecasting prefer Net30. If AcmeTech requires Net45, we can accept Net45 in the order form on two conditions: (1) a one-time activation credit (see commercial below), and (2) invoice remittance instructions confirmed in Appendix B.

- True-up: Redwood proposes quarterly true-ups with settlement applied to the next invoice cycle. We need to define the measurement window (we prefer calendar quarter). If AcmeTech's fiscal quarter differs we can map accordingly but need explicit language.

- Minimum commit proration & activation fees: We'll prorate the first period to the effective date. If you want a 05/01 anchor then provide the start date and we'll reflect that in the activation schedule.

I've attached our redline (orderform_redline.pdf) that highlights the exact wording changes we propose. If you can produce the VAT cert and confirm the fiscal vs calendar quarter question, we can circulate a DocuSign-ready Order Form.

Attachments: orderform_redline.pdf (pdf, 182KB)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Kim / Ben —

Thanks for the redline. Attached is our VAT/residency certificate and company tax information (tax_cert_acme.pdf). We confirm AcmeTech will accept calendar-quarter true-ups but would like the invoice settlement to occur within the first billing cycle of the next quarter.

On Net45: procurement can agree to Net45 if Redwood offers a small activation credit (AcmeTech needs better cashflow in the first 90 days). Would Redwood consider a $50k credit applied to the first invoice if we take Net45? That would address our finance team's cashflow constraints.

We reviewed your redline and are generally comfortable; our legal team will do minor edits but nothing material. We are happy to proceed to DocuSign once the credit/net-terms language is confirmed.

Attachments: tax_cert_acme.pdf (pdf, 124KB)

Best,
Oliver
